verdict.rationale: Unreal Engine ships built-in source-control integration with Perforce and SVN. Through it, the assets and code that make up editor automations (Python scripts, Blueprints) get change history and can be rolled back to earlier versions. However, this is general project versioning that depends on an external VCS, not automation-specific lifecycle management, and nothing documents a review step for automation changes. Missing for 10: automation-specific versioning, a documented review/diff workflow for automation changes, rollback that does not depend on an external Perforce/SVN server, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: providing a backup and history of changes so any files can be rolled back to an earlier version if something went wrong with the file
Unreal Engine comes with two fully-integrated methods that allow people to work together on their projects using version control software like Perforce and SVN.
